Hi Samir — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and next steps on pricing assumptions + caching so we can align on effective unit economics: 

Key points from the call:
- Expected monthly token volume: 200M–1B tokens (you mentioned pilot ~200M/mo, planned scale to 1B within 6–9 months)
- Target budget range: $10k–$40k/mo for staging -> scale depending on SLA and feature set
- Primary workload: product Q&A + personalized recommendations (short user messages + 100–800 token responses)

Caching / pricing follow-ups I promised:
1) Provide hit-rate scenarios (30% / 50% / 70%) and effective $/1M tokens after cache wins
2) Explain prefix cache strategy (what we cache, typical TTL, effect on request tokens)
3) Share a short spreadsheet with worked examples (attached)

Quick answers inline: 
- Baseline model price: assume $25 per 1M tokens for the open model variant we discussed (this is the list price used for our example; actual price varies by model).
- Effective cost with caching: effective $/1M = list_price * (1 - hit_rate). So with a 70% hit rate on your workload, effective cost ~ $7.50 per 1M tokens.

Notes on hit rates:
- Retrieval-heavy flows (many repeated system prompts + reused context chunks) commonly see 60–80% prefix hits.
- Freeform chat with long, unique user history tends to be 20–40%.
- Your described workload (short prompts, many repeated UI-driven templates + product ids) suggests we should model 50–70% as a realistic mid-case.

I attached a small calc sheet showing per-tier examples and what billing looks like at 200M / 500M / 1B tokens. Please review and tell me which scenario you want us to price formally for a committed Dedicated quote.

Next steps:
- Samir: confirm which volume line we should price (200M vs 500M vs 1B) and whether you need an SLA.
- Marcus / Aditya: we may need a short Dedicated estimate if they want a committed discount (Samir indicated procurement favors annual commit).

Thanks — Marissa

Great Qs — answers below and I updated the attached sheet with the 500M row for 50% and 70% hit rates. See tab "Worked examples."

1) What we cache: two primary forms — 
   - Prefix (system prompts + static instruction templates + product/context chunk): these are high-value for hits because they are identical across many requests. Typical prefix sizes you described (50–800 tokens) are perfect candidates.
   - KV-cache for decoder state: benefits repeated continuation of the exact same generation; less common in interactive web UIs.

2) Partial hits: we treat a request as a "cache hit" for the tokens that match a cached prefix. Billing is based on tokens submitted to the model after cache application. Example: if your raw request would be 800 tokens total and a cached prefix covers 500 tokens, the model processes 300 tokens and you are billed for ~300 model tokens (plus we surface the cache delta in logs). In our simplified pricing examples we express hit rate as fraction of total tokens eliminated by caching (not just request count).

Worked example (from sheet, baseline price = $25 / 1M tokens):
- 500M raw tokens/mo, 50% token-level hit rate -> billed tokens = 250M -> effective $/1M raw tokens = ($25 * 250M / 500M) = $12.50 per 1M
- 500M raw tokens/mo, 70% token-level hit rate -> billed tokens = 150M -> effective $/1M raw tokens = ($25 * 150M / 500M) = $7.50 per 1M

Other practical notes:
- Cache TTL: for product-context chunks we typically set a TTL of 24–72 hours for freshness; for system/static prompts TTL is effectively infinite until changed. TTLs will affect steady-state hit rates during high churn periods.
- Cold-start: expect a lower hit rate during initial rollout / small pilot; steady-state hit rate improves as popular items get primed in cache.
- Measurement: we recommend running a 2-week tracing window (we can share a lightweight tracing script) to get real hit-rate telemetry before finalizing committed pricing.

I've cc'd Marcus and Aditya for a committed/discounted Dedicated quote if they want to propose an annual commit at 500M/mo. Marcus — can you own preparing a rough Dedicated estimate and suggested discount tiers? Aditya — can you share the quick tracing script?

Thanks,
Marissa
